profile.campus: Forest City, Rutherford County, North Carolina (Meta's Forest City data center campus, Meta's second-ever data center after Prineville, Oregon)
profile.address: Solon David Smart Memorial Highway, Rutherford County, North Carolina, 28043
profile.reading: This Meta data center building (building 3 of 4 mapped in this cluster, westernmost to easternmost ordering) is part of Meta's Forest City campus in Rutherford County, North Carolina, Meta's second company-built data center after Prineville, Oregon. Facebook announced the original 300,000-square-foot building in November 2010, committing $450 million over five years and buying 150 acres of land on the site of a former manufacturing facility whose existing 44kV and 12.5kV power infrastructure and water capacity helped attract the project, per Data Center Knowledge's reporting at the time; construction was expected to take about 18 months, putting the first building online around 2012. Facebook chose Forest City in part to give it an East Coast counterpart to its West Coast data centers and to join Google and Apple, which had already built major facilities in the same part of western North Carolina. Facebook announced a second Forest City building in October 2011, and a third, roughly 480,000-square-foot building in October 2015 backed by more than $200 million in additional capital investment and a commitment to retain more than 125 full-time jobs, per the Rutherford County Economic Development Commission; that expansion also included more than $575,000 in local school and nonprofit funding and a partnership to provide free Wi-Fi to students and families. Meta's own current fact sheet for the campus reports more than $750 million invested overall, groundbreaking dated to 2010, roughly 275 operational jobs once complete, hundreds of peak skilled-trade construction workers, more than $5.9 million in direct funding to local schools and nonprofits, and a Meta-supported project adding 310 megawatts of new renewable energy in North Carolina, alongside Meta's standard LEED Gold, 100%-renewable-electricity, and water-positive-by-2030 commitments. Meta does not publish a specific street address, current building count, or per-building square footage for individual Forest City structures on its fact sheet; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

profile.capacity_note: Meta does not publish per-building IT capacity, exact current square footage, or a confirmed building count for the Forest City campus; historical announcements describe an original 300,000-square-foot building (2010), a second building (2011), and a 480,000-square-foot third building (2015). No current per-building figure is asserted here.

profile.regional_context: Rutherford County sits in the broader western North Carolina data center corridor that also includes Google's Lenoir campus and Apple's Maiden campus, a cluster regional economic-development groups such as the Rutherford County EDC have promoted as a hub for large technology capital investment tied to available industrial land and Duke Energy's regional transmission infrastructure.

reading.body:
Meta's Forest City campus in Rutherford County has invested $750M+ since breaking ground in 2010 and operates with 275+ permanent staff. The campus achieves LEED Gold certification and sources 100 percent renewable energy matched to its operational electricity use. Meta has committed $5.9M+ to local schools and nonprofits and is supporting a 310 megawatt renewable energy addition to North Carolina's grid as part of its net-zero operations pledge.

The specific power capacity of this campus is not published by Meta. Without a stated megawatt figure, the campus cannot be ranked against other AI training facilities or assessed for its contribution to North Carolina's data center load. Among 19 mapped facilities in the state, only five publish power specifications, and this campus is not among them.

In North Carolina's published capacity landscape of 50 MW total across five disclosed facilities, the absence of a megawatt figure leaves this $750M+ investment unquantified as an AI infrastructure asset. The campus remains invisible to grid planning and AI scaling analysis despite its scale as a hyperscale operator's major regional investment.
